cand.title: Land & Development Conference 2027
cand.ledgerVenue: Metro Toronto Convention Centre, North Building, 255 Front Street West, Toronto

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Roelof van Dijk is listed as Deputy Managing Director, North America Real Estate & Construction Group – Global Finance, Informa Connect; his profile also describes him as Executive Director of Real Estate Forums. He is the senior organizer relationship/routing contact. Maria Encarnacion is the event’s named general-inquiries contact and a practical first route to the accommodation procurement lead. Frank Scalisi is listed on this event’s contact page with SponsorREForums@informa.com; a separate official portfolio page identifies him as Director of Sales for named Buildings Show products. He is relevant for sponsorship/partner introductions, not a verified housing buyer. Anne Naumyk is the named speaker-enquiries contact, relevant to asking who handles speaker lodging. None is publicly identified as the person with hotel-contract signature authority.
findings.futureEdition: June 10, 2027 is officially announced by both organizer and venue, within the requested horizon. One-day edition in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Venue listing gives June 10 only; start and end dates are both 2027-06-10. The organizer header incorrectly labels the date Wednesday; use the numeric date corroborated by MTCC, not that weekday. No official exact 2028 edition announcement was located.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications: the Harbourfront/downtown location and MTCC access suit selected out-of-town delegates, speakers, executives and small side meetings. The 157-room property is not a credible sole conference venue or exclusive housing solution for the published 900+ audience; its approximately 240-theatre largest room cannot host that plenary. Pursue a right-sized sub-block only after the organizer supplies actual non-local and speaker demand; no room allocation is evidenced. This is a city-convention lodging proposition, not a resort retreat. Do not promise catering, restaurant/lounge access or receptions until current operations are verified.
findings.venueCommitments: Metro Toronto Convention Centre, North Building, 255 Front Street West, Toronto, Ontario M5V 2W6, Canada. This is downtown Toronto proper, within the hotel’s MTCC territory, not a resort or a competing hotel. Both organizer directions and the venue calendar confirm the published venue; the underlying contract is not public.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified editions: May 13, 2014; May 28, 2024; June 5, 2025; May 27, 2026 — all MTCC North Building, Toronto. June 10, 2027 is the next announced edition. These observations show repeat Toronto/MTCC use, not destination rotation. The 2014 brochure calls it the 10th annual conference; 2024 was the 20th anniversary. This is not a complete intervening-year timeline and does not establish a 2028 date.
findings.accommodationSourcing: The 2027-headed Hotel & Travel page states: “Informa does not work with outside companies for hotel needs, but rather directly with the hotels to secure room blocks.” It also states: “Reservations can be made directly with the hotels via the respective websites above.” This establishes a published direct-hotel sourcing policy, not an open RFP. However, the accessible page and hotel-map page expose no named hotels, rates, cutoffs, allocations or usable edition-specific hotel booking links. Every currently named 2027 hotel: none identifiable in the reviewed official material. Consequently, 2027 block execution, incumbent hotels and ability to add suppliers remain unconfirmed; no housing bureau is verified. Separately, the 2014 brochure names Intercontinental Toronto Centre at $189 plus tax, with an April 2, 2014 reservation deadline. That is historical only, not a 2027 commitment.
findings.organizationStructure: Commercial corporate event under Informa Connect / Canadian Real Estate Forums, not an association-owned congress. Canadian Real Estate Forums is wholly owned by Informa PLC. MTCC is the venue, not the organizer or lodging buyer. The published accommodation policy describes Informa dealing directly with hotels; no separately appointed PCO, DMC or housing bureau was verified for this edition.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Conference space is already allocated to MTCC, so do not pitch displacement of the main event. The official travel page claims “Availability is extremely limited and prices are increasing daily,” but provides no dated hotel-level inventory evidence; this is not verified overflow or proof of an incumbent sellout. Intercontinental Toronto Centre is documented only for 2014. No named 2027 incumbent, exclusive lodging arrangement, room-night total, pickup or overflow requirement was verified. Attendance is not equivalent to overnight room demand.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Maria Encarnacion at REForums@informa.com, copying Roelof.vanDijk@informa.com, with a concise MTCC-adjacent Harbourfront lodging proposal. Ask who owns 2027 accommodation contracting, which hotels/blocks are contracted, expected non-local and speaker room demand, stay dates, cutoffs, pickup and whether another hotel can be considered. Offer a modest tailored block only after demand and hotel availability are confirmed; do not assert an RFP. If 2027 is closed, request the next sourcing review and an introduction to the hotel procurement lead. Route speaker-lodging questions through Anne.Naumyk@informa.com if appropriate. Verify the hotel’s restaurant/lounge and catered-event capability before adding food-and-beverage promises.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: 2027 is an accessible organizer-contact path, not a verified open hotel procurement opportunity. Venue is confirmed; hotel sourcing is unconfirmed. The published direct-hotel policy provides a plausible introduction route, but neither procurement timing nor willingness to add Radisson Blu is established. No evidence supports classifying the edition as fully committed elsewhere or sourcing open.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: repeat Toronto/MTCC use makes a multi-edition accommodation-supplier relationship worth developing if 2027 blocks are closed. Ask for the next hotel review cycle and performance requirements rather than asserting a 2028 event or open inventory. The historical Intercontinental relationship is a useful incumbent question, not evidence of a current competitive contract.
